findings.title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but events only get sample_rate
findings.body: upsampled_count() is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)), and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to that function. The only ingest/test path added in this PR, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate and never sets sample_weight. A client_sample_rate of 0.1 must become a weight of 10 (1/rate) to match the new stats test, which expects count == 10 for one stored error. As written, allowlisted error stats either sum a missing/null column (count collapses toward 0, or the query errors) or, if sample_weight were copied from sample_rate, would report 0.1 instead of 10. toInt64 also truncates any fractional weight. Error volume on the events-stats API would be wrong for every allowlisted project.

findings.title: Error detection is a substring check on the original request, not the executed query
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query returns true when the raw request.GET query string contains the substring event.type:error. That matches negated filters such as !event.type:error, so a discover query that explicitly excludes errors is still rewritten from count() to upsampled_count()/sum(sample_weight). The check also ignores the query string actually executed: _get_event_stats passes the closed-over request into is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, not the query argument. Dashboard discover-split builds transactions_only_query / errors_only_query and still calls _get_event_stats with the original request, so a request whose query contains event.type:error will upsample the transaction-only split query (sample_weight is not valid for transactions), and an errors-only split of a query that does not contain that substring will not upsample. Counts will be wrong or the Snuba query will fail.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset, not the dataset that runs
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the endpoint's outer dataset, while _get_event_stats runs scoped_dataset, which dashboard widget splitting can change to discover or back to the metrics dataset. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns true for the errors module unconditionally and false for transactions. If the outer dataset is errors but the executed dataset is discover/transactions (or the reverse), count() is rewritten, or not rewritten, for the wrong dataset. Transaction queries can then reference sample_weight, and error queries can keep a raw count() and under-report volume.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key uses process-local hash and is never invalidated
findings.body: The cache key is error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(sorted project ids)} with a 60s TTL. hash() is salted per process for non-int values, and even for ints it is not a stable cross-version key; workers will miss or collide, so the stated cross-request cache does not work. invalidate_upsampling_cache builds the same key but is never called when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes, so a stale True remains for up to 60s and keeps rewriting count() after a project is removed from the allowlist (and a stale False keeps serving un-upsampled counts after it is added). Integration tests patch options.get but do not clear this cache, so a reused project id can make the allowlist tests assert the wrong count.

findings.title: store_event copies client_sample_rate into sample_rate without inverting
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling sets normalized_data['sample_rate'] = float(client_sample_rate) whenever the value is truthy. Sampling rate and sample weight are inverses: 0.1 means one stored event represents ten. Writing the rate into sample_rate (and not sample_weight) makes every later store_event path, not just these tests, persist the wrong magnitude. A rate of 0 is also dropped by the truthiness check, so a fully sampled client is stored with no sample_rate at all.
